_about: The in-level HUD and the start of a level, as the original draws them: the two walk
pads, restart and pause, the clear-portals button, and the black fade, the 'Part N'
caption and the current-score plaque every level opens with. Read by sim/Hud.hpp.
EVERY POSITION AND SIZE IS IN DESIGN UNITS, which in this port are the level's own
pixels: the view is view.json's height_px (256) tall and follows the window's shape
across. The original draws both its world and its UI at 2.8125 screen px per unit at
720p (720 / 256). Each element is anchored to the SCREEN CORNER it was measured from,
because 1280 / 2.8125 = 455.11 is not a whole number and the view's width changes with
the window: an element anchored from the wrong edge drifts off its corner.
TWO SOURCES, and every block names which it took each number from.
MEASURED - captures of the original at 1280x720, analysed in the remake's gitignored
out/parity/specs/ui1/static_hud.md (+ .json) and level_start_timeline.md (+ .json).
DECODED - the original's compiled script, android_game.bin, by function and byte
range, read the way every other data file here cites it. The listing is not
committed: it is the original's code.
The decode's g_scale.scale(N) IS N units at any screen: the plaque below is decoded at
scale(40, 40) and measured with its centre at (40.02, 40.02) units, and the ring's decoded
scale(200) grows at the 167 units/s the captures bracket.
Where the two disagree, docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md step 38 says
which was taken and why. Nothing here is Asantee's: numbers only, never the art.
EVERY ALPHA HERE IS A DISPLAY-SPACE ALPHA, as the original blended: the layer draws all of
it through the engine's screen overlay (src/core/ScreenOverlay.hpp), after the tone map, so
a translucent control mixes over the encoded picture at exactly its alpha whatever is behind
it. Drawn through the scene as it was until step 39, white came out at 186 and a 0.47 button
read 0.32..0.56 by background (step 39 has the table).

DECODED, which is why it is where it is although it is a level entity at (-61, -24):
ETHCallback_no_portal_sign (MiscCallbacks.angelscript, bytes 343129..343339) calls
followUp(thisEntity, GetCameraPos() + GetSize() * 0.5, 600, 100, true) every frame.
followUp (utilEntityEffect.angelscript, bytes 328407..329130) builds a
PositionInterpolator from where the entity stands to that target over interpStride
(600 ms), filtered by smoothEnd, on accumulated frame time; each frame, when the target
is not where the entity is and switchTime > updateRate (100 ms), it resets the
interpolator from its current position to the target and zeroes switchTime; then it
adds the frame's time to both and puts the entity at the interpolator's position. So
the sign's centre trails the camera's top-left corner by half its own size. It is
found by the level's own metadata/entity_name, which is how SeekEntity finds it in
PortalManager::PortalManager (instruction 118).

_clock: TWO CLOCKS, as the original has them (step 40). Zero at the tick a level is loaded, the
LEVEL'S AGE times everything here but the black: the caption (Ethanon's ETHTextDrawer::Draw
GetLastFrameElapsedTime), the pads' slide and pulse (ScreenPad::update, bytes
150164..151039, instruction 170: g_timeManager's last frame time) and the sign's follow.
The black is the only part timed by GetTime(), a live CLOCK_MONOTONIC read
(AndroidGLES2Video.cpp:66-70) - see overlay.start_after_ms for what that costs it.
A retry opens the same way: its restart builds a fresh Game state.

_source: DECODED: a FadeInController (ETHFramework/FadeInController.angelscript, bytes
37911..38779) draws a full-screen black rect at alpha uint((1 - elapsed / time) * 255)
until elapsed reaches time = 700 ms, and a level has TWO of them: BaseState::preLoop
(bytes 11137..11245) adds one and Game::preLoop adds another (instruction 316). Two
linear blacks stacked leave (elapsed / 700)^2 of the picture.
MEASURED, and reconciled by that: level_start_timeline fitted a linear 0.54 s fade
(1.855 /s, section 1). The same frames fit (t / 0.7)^2 with the start a steady
0.19 +-0.03 s before its black frame, where the linear fit's implied start drifts by
0.13 s across the ramp. Both cover the world, the player, restart and pause and the
plaque; one covers the pads (below); neither covers the caption.
_between: DECODED, and it explains the one thing level_start_timeline could not: the PADS are
drawn BETWEEN the two blacks. BaseState::preLoop adds the UI layer manager (restart,
pause, the plaque) and then the first FadeInController; Game::preLoop adds the
character - whose draw is the pads - long before the second (instruction 316); and
GameControllerManager::draw draws its controllers in the order they were added. So the
world, the buttons and the plaque are under both, the pads under one, and 'Part N',
which DrawFadingText hands to the engine's own drawable manager, over both. The
timeline measured the pads 'brighter than under the overlay (17-49 grey) and darker
than above it (89-155)' at 1.695..1.727 s: under one of two.
_start_after: HOW LONG BOTH BLACKS STAY WHOLLY BLACK before their 700 ms begin, on the level's age.
DECODED, which is why there is such a number: FadeInController::FadeInController and
::start (bytes 37911..38429) take startTime from GetTime() - wall time - after a
LoadSprite, and ::draw fades by GetTime() - startTime. Game::preLoop builds the second
at instruction 316 and BaseState::preLoop the first; Ethanon runs preLoop only once the
scene is built (ETHEngine.cpp:176-179 -> ETHScriptWrapper::LoadScene, .Scene.cpp:570-612,
then LoadSceneScripts :660-668), all inside ONE frame's update. Every other part of the
opening accumulates FRAME time (see _clock), and gs2d charges a frame the whole wall
time since the last one, capped at 1000 ms (ComputeElapsedTimeF, Application.cpp:36-50;
android/main.cpp:180-181). So the frame after a level's load carries all of that load
in its delta for the caption, the plaque, the pads and the sign, and the black only
what came after instruction 316.
MEASURED on rec11, the only footage of an opening: each lit frame n28..n37 gives the
level's age from its caption (alpha = 1 - t / 3000) and the black's from the world's
brightness (k = (t / 700)^2), and the second runs behind the first by 465 ms
(level_start_timeline.md sections 1-2: median 465, 423..490; review 2's own table of
the same frames: median 464; step 40's re-measure from the raw frames with its own
reference: median 473). Its black frame n27 is the level's age 24 ms, black whole.
IT IS THAT EMULATOR'S LOAD, NOT A DESIGNED WAIT: a device that loaded a level in no
time would show 0. It is kept because it is what the original shows - pads home, plaque
up and 'Part N' dimmer before the picture comes through - and 0 here gives the
zero-load opening step 38 built.

_about: THE TWO ANIMATION PRIMITIVES every UI layer the original raises over a level is built from:
the pause here, and the finished, lost and help screens after it. Read by sim/UiLayer.hpp.
Specified in the remake's gitignored out/parity/specs/ui2/spec.md section 0.4 (numbers from
pause_finished.md and popups_gameover.md beside it).
BOTH RUN ON UI FRAME TIME, which the pause does not stop: a layer animates while the game
is frozen under it (spec section 0.3). The port keeps that clock per layer, on the tick.

_about: THE PAUSE SCREEN, CustomGameMenuLayer (extends GameMenuLayer and SoundPanelLayer), which the
in-level pause control and the back key raise over the frozen level. Read by sim/Pause.hpp.
Specified in the remake's gitignored out/parity/specs/ui2/spec.md section 2; its evidence is
pause_finished.md section 1 (+ .json) beside it. Measured on pause_fresh_1-1.png and
pause_gold_1-4.png, 1280x720, 3 s after the tap.
PLACED BY FRACTIONS OF THE SCREEN, NOT FROM CORNERS (spec 0.1): each element's anchor is
view * at_screen, and its top-left is that anchor less size_units * origin. Sizes stay in
units, so at another aspect the x positions move with the width and the sizes do not. The
switches and Achievements are flush in their corners only because their fraction is 0 or 1
with the matching origin. Every size is the sprite's 1x texel size in units; the hd twin is
what is drawn (spec 0.1).
ALPHAS ARE DISPLAY-SPACE, drawn through the engine's screen overlay after restart, pause and
the level's blacks and before the level-start caption (spec 2.2).

_about: HOW A LEVEL ENDS: the beat after the door or the death, the HUD going, and the two screens
the original raises over the level that is still running - LevelFinishedLayer and
LevelLostLayer. Read by sim/LevelEnd.hpp, over ui_layer's primitives.
Specified in the remake's gitignored out/parity/specs/ui2/spec.md sections 3 and 4, and its
deltas D1..D9 (section 1.2); the evidence is pause_finished.md sections 2..3 and
popups_gameover.md section 4 beside it. Measured on finished_1-1.png, finish_1-1.mp4,

GetTimeF() read, takes the layer's own tick clock since it attached.
